reviews.body:
The swap itself is right. OpenAI's deprecations page lists `gpt-5-mini` for shutdown on 2026-12-11 with `gpt-5.6-terra` as the replacement, and apart from the items below every hunk is a plain ID swap. It changes the `AgentConfig.model` default, so it'll get a release note.

Before merging:
- The PR description is about a different project (`settings.json`, `openai.js`, `gpt-4-turbo`). Please replace it with what this PR does.
- `providers.md` goes beyond the retirement: it drops `gpt-5` and `gpt-5-nano` and recommends `gpt-5.6-sol` for tool use. Please limit it to replacing `gpt-5-mini`, or link the deprecation entries that back the rest.
- `main_stdio.py`: the comment there was already garbled, and a dated retirement note will go stale. Please either match the sibling clients (`main_sse.py` and `main_stdio_async.py` use `gpt-5.1`, with a comment saying why) or remove the comment.
- `test_default_model_is_current_openai_id` only pins a string literal. Please rename it to say that, or drop it.

comments.body:
The description now matches this pull request. `providers.md` only replaces `gpt-5-mini`; `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-nano`, and the tool-use line stay as they were. The dated note in `main_stdio.py` is removed and the field stays `gpt-5.6-terra`, the listed replacement for `gpt-5-mini`. The default-model test is renamed to `test_default_model_pins_string_gpt_5_6_terra` because it only pins that string.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
